statements.quote: The scientific divergent application task (SDAT) was adapted from the instrument developed by Wan et al. (2025), consisting of 10 items involving various novel materials, such as graphene, carbon fiber, and glass microspheres. Each item provided a brief introduction to a specific material and asked participants to generate novel applications for it. In the present study, three items were randomly selected as experimental materials: transparent ceramics, electronic skin, and crystal resin.

The landing page, DOI resolver, preprint metadata, files-provider endpoint, primary-file endpoint, OSF storage listing and PDF download all returned HTTP 200. Its has_data_links is "no", data_links is [], has_prereg_links is "not_applicable", and prereg_links is []. This statement is repository metadata, not text in the saved PDF. notes: Checked 2026-10-09. Read all 374 lines of the markdown conversion, including the complete references, and verified quoted passages against text extracted with pymupdf from the corresponding PDF pages. The source is the 31-page EdArXiv v2 preprint; it ends with references and contains no appendix, formal data/code-availability statement, preregistration link, access-on-request offer, or c147 repository URL. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are empty. Statements above include relevant materials provenance, supplement pointers, recorded-text and software information; these are not promises of data sharing. The manuscript refers to Supplementary Figure 2A and 2B, while main-text Figure 2 presents the two classification schemes. No separate supplement was listed with either preprint version, so it remains unconfirmed whether the references intend separate files. The cited OSF link https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/dy9p8_v1 was checked (HTTP 200, redirects to https://osf.io/dy9p8_v1). https://api.osf.io/v2/preprints/dy9p8_v1/ and its files/osfstorage/?page[size]=100 and relationships/node/ endpoints all returned HTTP 200: the Wan et al. source contains only Measurement and Automated Scoring of Scientific Creative Thinking.pdf (932435 bytes), no linked supplemental node, and no data links. It is the SDAT instrument source for a different paper, not a deposit of c147 observations, and is excluded from the deposit count. The only confirmed public c147 repository object is a manuscript; this is not classified as public_partial or code_or_materials_only merely because it prints group summaries or explains methods. OSF explicitly says c147 data are not publicly available because of ongoing analysis and ethical restrictions, but provides no confirmed account, approval or request route; therefore status is none_found rather than assuming on_request or restricted access. No public c147 rows or columns were available to inspect. We cannot compute participant-level means, SDs, SEs, outcome-specific analyzed counts, within-person dependence or diversity from full participant ideas. The open items on creativity-score aggregation, model observation counts/dependence, covariate specifications and differences from PROCESS total effects remain unresolved, as do sequence allocation and exclusion-stage/partner handling. Medium confidence reflects the inaccessible newer Wiley version: its data policy or supplementary material may differ from the preprint. No account, access request, CAPTCHA bypass, or author contact was attempted; all remote file reads stayed in memory.
